title: Free bar, uniform heating
description: Steel bar 100 x 20 x 10 mm, every face at 120 °C, stress-free at 20 °C (dT = 100 K). The faces x = 0, y = 0 and z = 0 are sliding supports: statically determinate, so the bar expands freely.

quantities.label: Free thermal elongation
quantities.citation: J. M. Gere, B. J. Goodno, Mechanics of Materials, 8th ed., Cengage 2013, Section 2.5, thermal effects
quantities.tolerance_reason: Free uniform expansion is a linear displacement field, exact for any mesh; the band catches a support that restrains the bar.

quantities.label: Peak von Mises stress (zero in theory; error relative to E alpha dT, the stress of a fully clamped bar)
quantities.citation: J. M. Gere, B. J. Goodno, Mechanics of Materials, 8th ed., Cengage 2013, Section 2.5, thermal effects (a statically determinate structure carries no thermal stress)
quantities.tolerance_reason: Any stress means the supports restrain the expansion; 2 % of the clamped-bar stress (about 5 MPa) is the band.
